title: Pseudo-coherence is invariant under nilpotent quotient
statement: Let $R'\to R$ be a surjective map of commutative rings whose kernel is a nilpotent ideal. For $K'\in D(R')$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], put $K=K'\otimes_{R'}^L R$ using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] if and only if $K'$ is pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: Identify B with A/I for I=ker φ using the quotient-kernel ring equivalence. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies extension along φ followed by restriction along this equivalence with extension along A→A/I. Postcomposition of right Kan extensions by an equivalence preserves universality: the induced functor on right-extension categories is an equivalence and preserves terminal objects. Thus transport of the given universal derived pair is legitimate, with no choice of a new derived tensor object.

For the forward implication choose the bounded-above finite-free model P given by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Raise A and B by ULift to the module universe. Restriction along these ring equivalences preserves the upper bound and transports bases; uniqueness of left adjoints supplies the ordinary scalar-extension comparison. Transport the universal derived counit using the homotopy and derived equivalences and right Kan extension uniqueness. The raised complex is termwise free, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], and is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. Apply the module counit theorem [lem-pc-kflat-scalar-extension-counit]. All comparison maps are isomorphisms, and the target equivalence reflects isomorphisms, so the original counit is invertible on P. Termwise extension has the same upper bound and finite bases. Compose the counit comparison with the derived model isomorphism to obtain a finite-free model of L(K').

For the reverse implication choose a bounded-above finite-free B-complex E representing L(K'). Restrict its scalars through A/I≅B; transport its finite bases by the ring equivalence and preserve its upper bound. Its terms are projective by [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-projective]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-projective-complex-lift] to the transported universal pair, this prescribed reduced complex, and K'. This supplies a bounded-above projective A-complex P representing K', with termwise reduction isomorphic to the transported E. Hence each reduced P term is finite free.

Fix a term M of P. Choose a finite basis of (A/I)⊗M and let F be the free A-module on that basis index. The quotient map M→(A/I)⊗M is surjective by the tensor/quotient equivalence. Projectivity of the free source F [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] lifts the reduced basis isomorphism to a map F→M. Tensor extensionality proves that the base-changed map is the basis isomorphism. Convert tensor reduction to quotient reduction and apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent] to get surjectivity without finiteness of M. Therefore M is finite.

Since I is nilpotent, every 1+x with x∈I is a unit: its image in A/I is 1, and units lift modulo a nilpotent ideal. The term M is now finite and projective, and its reduction is free. Apply the already proved criterion [lem-sc-finite-projective-free-mod-ideal] to conclude M is free. This reuses the projective splitting/isomorphism-lifting argument rather than reproving the kernel calculation. Empty bases and the zero ring are included.

Apply these module arguments in each degree of P. The lifted complex retains its upper bound and its derived identification with K'; its terms are now finite free. The definition [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] gives pseudo-coherence of K', completing the equivalence.
